notes: §1985:XIV.3.5.4 GR1: for an input CD "the contents of the data items specified by data-name-1 (SYMBOLIC QUEUE) through data-name-4 (SYMBOLIC SUB-QUEUE-3) ... designate the queue structure containing the message". MessageControlSession.Receive reads the four 12-character names at positions 1-48 (CommunicationArea.QueuePath, whatever the user's record calls them), MessageDefinitions.FindQueue resolves them as a prefix of the hierarchy (blank lower levels let the MCS choose, a level below a blank one or an unknown name is status 20), and TakeFromQueue takes from that structure; the facility has no edition arm at 85. The witness is status 20 for an unknown queue. Probes at --std 85 (classes a, b, d, f): Q1 alone took Q1/S1 and filled IN-S1 with S1 (§1985:XIV.2.2.4 GR5); Q1/S2 took S2-MSG; Q1/S2/T1 took T1-MSG; Q1/blank/T1, Q1/NOSUCH and an all-blank queue each gave status 20 with WITH DATA run and the receiver unchanged; ref-mod BUF(10:1), BUF(1:N) and an OCCURS DEPENDING ON group received the next portions correctly.

next.reason: 1985: "the contents of the data items specified by data-name-1 (SYMBOLIC QUEUE) through data-name-4 (SYMBOLIC SUB-QUEUE-3) ... designate the queue structure"; 2023: "Input CDs and queues are gone; 2023 RECEIVE uses a message tag: "Data-name-1 shall be the name of a message-tag data item."". The 2023 RECEIVE takes messages between run units, identified by a message tag. It has no input CD or symbolic queue/sub-queue fields, so the 1985 queue-designation rule is gone.
